why: Take or skip on a line: for each house you either rob it (and add the best up to two houses back) or skip it (and keep the best up to the previous house), so best[i] = max(best[i-1], best[i-2] + nums[i]).
hints: Look at the last house. Either you rob it or you do not. What does each choice leave you with?
best[i] = max(best[i-1], best[i-2] + nums[i]): skip house i, or take it and fall back to the best answer two houses earlier.
Only the last two values matter, so keep two variables and roll them. O(n) time, O(1) space.
pitfalls: Greedily taking every other house (even or odd positions) is wrong: [2,1,1,9] wants houses 0 and 3.
A single house is its own answer.
